t_5d6035b1e800:0397b16:1:6.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Puan Yinsu (普菴印肅禪師語錄), Puan Yinsu's extended instruction. Puan Yinsu is the exact narrator who says that Li Tongxuan, the Huayan Treatise Lord, deeply praised the open-ground white ox in the Lotus Sutra; Li is the person discussed, not the speaker of this turn.

t_d065698c14a8:0462a07:1:3.AttributionNote: Essentials of Chan Master Foguo Keqin (佛果克勤禪師心要). The complete instruction is Yuanwu Keqin's own direct address: Yuanwu says that resting until not one thought arises brings release from sense-dust and conceptual imagining. No embedded speaker owns the stored line.

t_7cddddb76d37:0480a12:1:1.AttributionNote: Essentials of Chan Master Foguo Keqin (佛果克勤禪師心要), immediately before the instruction to State Grandmother Zhang. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker who describes functioning throughout the twelve hours without self and other, love and hate, gain and loss, coming and going, and quotes the saying about natural functioning.

t_9bdac4a01636:0535c02:1:3.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingan Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄). Yingan Tanhua is the exact speaker in this instruction: recalling his own former words to students, he says the clay pellet penetrates both principle and phenomena and calls this their complete interpenetration.

t_47e7132eb361:0539a21:1:5.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingan Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄). Yingan Tanhua is the exact speaker of the continuous instruction; he describes the genuine student as exposed at the gateways of the six sense faculties throughout day and night.

t_a38f997d9c16:0788b20:1:3.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jieshi Zhipeng (介石智朋禪師語錄), an ascent-seat exchange. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk, who contrasts discussing past and present as making rice by steaming sand and asks how to communicate beyond two failed routes. All six attribution rungs leave this monk without a personal name.

t_a38f997d9c16:0069b15:1:2.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chijue Daochong (痴絕道冲禪師語錄). Chijue Daochong is the exact speaker of the uninterrupted instruction: he compares intentional investigation and verbal theorizing to steaming sand to make rice and digging into earth to seek heaven.

t_5ce4bbfe682f:0193a04:1:8.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hengchuan Xinggong (橫川行珙禪師語錄). Hengchuan Xinggong explicitly raises a verse with 'Krakucchanda Buddha said'; Krakucchanda Buddha is therefore the exact quoted speaker of the headword-bearing line about realizing the original nature of body and mind as empty. Hengchuan follows with his own comment.

t_6e762a1da16f:0392a15:1:5.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Liao'an Qingyu (了菴清欲禪師語錄), volume nine, inscription on writings by Biefeng and Tudu. Liao'an Qingyu is the author and exact speaker of the inscription; he contrasts their uncontrived verse and letters with people glued to discriminating consciousness who busy themselves with literary carving.

t_b0d4b62a9c2f:0665c06:1:4.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yu'an Zhiji (愚菴智及禪師語錄). Yu'an Zhiji is the exact speaker: after the unnamed cook says that he has cut thirty patriarchs' heads while slicing melons, Yu'an asks which one has blood beneath its skin.

ActorAttribution.ActorLabel: an unnamed Chan practitioner from Jiahe
ActorAttribution.ActorRole: preserver and publisher of Daqian's record

t_ada407625f42:0699a15:2:2.AttributionNote: Drafts from Chan Master Weilin Daopei's Traveling Hermitage (為霖禪師旅泊菴稿), Weilin Daopei's preface to Daqian's recorded sayings. The exact grammatical actor is the Chan practitioner identified only as being from Jiahe: Weilin says that this practitioner had long trained under the hammer and whisk, cherished the record, and spread it widely. All six rungs supply no personal name for him.

t_659e88cc44d5:0737a23:1:5.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zongbao Daodu (宗寶道獨禪師語錄). Zongbao Daodu is the exact speaker in his sustained address to the community; he says the matter cannot be spoken despite everyone's effort and is only known personally as hot or cold and handled personally as urgent or slow.

t_63ee0f50447f:0739c02:1:5.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zongbao Daodu (宗寶道獨禪師語錄). Zongbao Daodu is the exact speaker of the hall instruction: he says ordinary meditation-hall practice is either torpor or agitation and makes those very states the students' place for establishing life.

t_927d274aa0fc:0772c05:1:4.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng (湛然圓澄禪師語錄). Zhanran Yuancheng is the exact speaker of the continuous admonition: he criticizes people who memorize two phrases from the ancients' expedient sayings and call that awakening to the Way or penetrating the lineage.

t_bcf65a900b7a:0814a14:1:1.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng (湛然圓澄禪師語錄), a question-and-answer unit. The exact headword-bearing speaker is the unnamed questioner who asks what 'afflictions are bodhi' means; Zhanran Yuancheng then answers by glossing bodhi as awareness. All six rungs leave the questioner unnamed.

t_bcf65a900b7a:0814a18:1:2.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng (湛然圓澄禪師語錄), the answer to an unnamed questioner. Zhanran Yuancheng is the exact speaker who says that because bodhi does not differ from afflictions, one recognizes afflictions as bodhi.

t_b437e79a4646:0816b10:1:2.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng (湛然圓澄禪師語錄). The source personally names Director of Education Fu Shangpan as the exact questioner: Fu says he has long exerted himself in Chan and had an awakening, but is not fluent when questioning and discriminating in response to the occasion, and asks where the fault lies. Zhanran answers him.

t_207efae5f6bd:0864c06:1:4.AttributionNote: Mailang Minghuai's Difficult Questions about the Chan Lineage (雲門麥浪懷禪師宗門設難). Mailang Minghuai is the exact answerer and expository speaker: responding to a question about live and dead phrases, he defines a dead phrase as one that falls into verbal explanation, a path of principle, conceptual thought, and discrimination. Xu Yuanzhao is the recorder, not the speaker.
